# oidc — OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect

[All groups](README.md)

## Every oidc operation

Every operation in this group also takes these.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--strict` | bool | Judge against the OAuth 2.0 Security BCP (RFC 9700): every recommendation it makes that is not met becomes a failure, so exit status 2 means the server or client setup falls short of it. |
| `--fapi` | bool | Judge against the FAPI 2.0 Security Profile: adds its requirements as checks (PAR, PKCE S256, private_key_jwt or mutual TLS, sender-constrained tokens, the iss response parameter, PS256/ES256/EdDSA) and implies strict. |

## oidc discover

Fetch an issuer's OpenID Connect discovery document (or RFC 8414 metadata), fetch its JWKS, and check both against the specifications and the OAuth 2.0 Security BCP.

MCP tool: `oidc_discover`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer URL, or the full .well-known metadata URL. **Required.** |

Plus the parameters [every oidc operation](#every-oidc-operation) takes and the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## oidc login

Run the Authorization Code flow with PKCE end to end: listen on a loopback redirect URI, open the browser, capture the authorization response, exchange the code, validate the ID token and call UserInfo. Flags a granted offline_access without a refresh token and granted scopes that yield no claims. Also handles implicit and hybrid response types. Blocks until the person finishes signing in.

MCP tool: `oidc_login`. Opens a browser and waits for a person.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer URL; endpoints and keys are discovered from its metadata. |
| `--client-id` | string | OAuth client identifier. |
| `--client-secret` | string | Client secret (prefer env IDPDBG_CLIENT_SECRET or a profile). Secret: falls back to `IDPDBG_CLIENT_SECRET`, redacted in traces. |
| `--client-auth` | string | Client authentication method; default basic when a secret is set, otherwise none. One of `basic`, `post`, `none`, `private_key_jwt`, `client_secret_jwt`, `tls_client_auth`, `self_signed_tls_client_auth`. |
| `--token-endpoint` | string | Token endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--client-key` | string | Client private key (PEM inline or a path) for private_key_jwt and signed request objects. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--client-key-id` | string | kid to put in the header of JWTs signed with client_key. |
| `--signing-alg` | string | JWS algorithm for client_key; default follows the key type (RS256, ES256, EdDSA); use PS256 for RSA-PSS. |
| `--client-assertion-aud` | string | aud of the client assertion; default is the issuer, else the endpoint being called. |
| `--mtls-cert` | string | Client certificate (PEM inline or a path) for mutual TLS. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--mtls-key` | string | Private key for mtls_cert (PEM inline or a path). May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--dpop` | bool | Send DPoP proofs (RFC 9449) so issued tokens are bound to a key. |
| `--dpop-key` | string | DPoP private key (PEM inline or a path); default is a fresh P-256 key that lasts for this run only. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--authorization-endpoint` | string | Authorization endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--scope` | string | Space-separated scopes. Default `openid profile email`. |
| `--response-type` | string | code (default), or an implicit/hybrid type such as 'code id_token'. Default `code`. |
| `--response-mode` | string | query, fragment or form_post. |
| `--pkce` | bool | Send an S256 PKCE challenge. Default `true`. |
| `--prompt` | string | none, login, consent or select_account. |
| `--login-hint` | string | Login hint passed to the provider. |
| `--acr-values` | string | Requested authentication context class references. |
| `--max-age` | int | Maximum authentication age in seconds. |
| `--audience` | string | audience parameter (Auth0-style APIs). |
| `--resource` | string | RFC 8707 resource indicator. |
| `--extra` | json | Extra authorization parameters as a JSON object, e.g. {"claims":"..."}. |
| `--par` | bool | Push the authorization request to the PAR endpoint first (RFC 9126) and send only its request_uri through the browser. |
| `--jar` | bool | Send the authorization parameters as a request object signed with client_key (RFC 9101). |
| `--pushed-authorization-request-endpoint` | string | PAR endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--redirect-host` | string | Host used in the redirect URI (localhost or 127.0.0.1). Default `localhost`. |
| `--redirect-port` | int | Loopback port to listen on. Default `8765`. |
| `--redirect-path` | string | Path of the redirect URI. Default `/callback`. |
| `--redirect-uri` | string | Full redirect URI, overriding host/port/path; must point at this machine. |
| `--open-browser` | bool | Open the system browser automatically. Default `true`. |
| `--wait` | int | Seconds to wait for the person to finish in the browser. Default `180`. |

Plus the parameters [every oidc operation](#every-oidc-operation) takes and the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## oidc device

Start the Device Authorization grant (RFC 8628) and return the user code and verification URL. With wait_for_user it keeps polling until the person approves; otherwise finish with oidc device_poll.

MCP tool: `oidc_device`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer URL; endpoints and keys are discovered from its metadata. |
| `--client-id` | string | OAuth client identifier. |
| `--client-secret` | string | Client secret (prefer env IDPDBG_CLIENT_SECRET or a profile). Secret: falls back to `IDPDBG_CLIENT_SECRET`, redacted in traces. |
| `--client-auth` | string | Client authentication method; default basic when a secret is set, otherwise none. One of `basic`, `post`, `none`, `private_key_jwt`, `client_secret_jwt`, `tls_client_auth`, `self_signed_tls_client_auth`. |
| `--token-endpoint` | string | Token endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--client-key` | string | Client private key (PEM inline or a path) for private_key_jwt and signed request objects. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--client-key-id` | string | kid to put in the header of JWTs signed with client_key. |
| `--signing-alg` | string | JWS algorithm for client_key; default follows the key type (RS256, ES256, EdDSA); use PS256 for RSA-PSS. |
| `--client-assertion-aud` | string | aud of the client assertion; default is the issuer, else the endpoint being called. |
| `--mtls-cert` | string | Client certificate (PEM inline or a path) for mutual TLS. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--mtls-key` | string | Private key for mtls_cert (PEM inline or a path). May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--dpop` | bool | Send DPoP proofs (RFC 9449) so issued tokens are bound to a key. |
| `--dpop-key` | string | DPoP private key (PEM inline or a path); default is a fresh P-256 key that lasts for this run only. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--scope` | string | Space-separated scopes. |
| `--device-authorization-endpoint` | string | Device authorization endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--wait-for-user` | bool | Poll the token endpoint until approved or the wait expires. |
| `--pkce` | bool | Send a PKCE code_challenge with the device authorization request and the code_verifier when polling, for servers that want it (Keycloak does for clients that require PKCE). |
| `--wait` | int | Seconds to keep polling. Default `300`. |

Plus the parameters [every oidc operation](#every-oidc-operation) takes and the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## oidc token_exchange

| `--audience` | string | Logical name of the target service. |

| `--dpop-key` | string | DPoP private key (PEM inline or a path); default is a fresh P-256 key that lasts for this run only. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--token` | string | Token to introspect. **Required.** CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--token-type-hint` | string | access_token or refresh_token. |
| `--introspection-endpoint` | string | Introspection endpoint, overriding discovery. |

Plus the parameters [every oidc operation](#every-oidc-operation) takes and the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## oidc revoke

Revoke a token (RFC 7009).

| `--client-auth` | string | Client authentication method; default basic when a secret is set, otherwise none. One of `basic`, `post`, `none`, `private_key_jwt`, `client_secret_jwt`, `tls_client_auth`, `self_signed_tls_client_auth`. |
| `--token-endpoint` | string | Token endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--client-key` | string | Client private key (PEM inline or a path) for private_key_jwt and signed request objects. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--client-key-id` | string | kid to put in the header of JWTs signed with client_key. |
| `--signing-alg` | string | JWS algorithm for client_key; default follows the key type (RS256, ES256, EdDSA); use PS256 for RSA-PSS. |

| `--mtls-key` | string | Private key for mtls_cert (PEM inline or a path). May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--dpop` | bool | Send DPoP proofs (RFC 9449) so issued tokens are bound to a key. |
| `--dpop-key` | string | DPoP private key (PEM inline or a path); default is a fresh P-256 key that lasts for this run only. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--token` | string | Token to revoke. **Required.** CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |

## oidc userinfo

Call the UserInfo endpoint with an access token. Given the ID token it checks that both describe the same subject; given the granted scopes it checks that each one actually yields its claims.

MCP tool: `oidc_userinfo`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer URL; endpoints and keys are discovered from its metadata. |
| `--access-token` | string | Access token with the openid scope. **Required.** CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--userinfo-endpoint` | string | UserInfo endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--id-token` | string | ID token whose sub the response must match. CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--scope` | string | Scopes that were granted; each of profile, email, phone and address is checked for its claims. |
| `--dpop` | bool | The access token is DPoP-bound: send it with a proof. |
| `--dpop-key` | string | The DPoP private key the token is bound to (PEM inline or a path). May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |

Plus the parameters [every oidc operation](#every-oidc-operation) takes and the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

Register a client with Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591 / OIDC DCR).

|---|---|---|
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer URL; endpoints and keys are discovered from its metadata. |
| `--registration-endpoint` | string | Registration endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--metadata` | json | Client metadata as JSON, e.g. {"client_name":"test","redirect_uris":["http://localhost:8765/callback"]} (CLI: @file). **Required.** |
| `--initial-access-token` | string | Initial access token, if the server requires one. Secret: falls back to `IDPDBG_INITIAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, redacted in traces. |

Read, update or delete a dynamically registered client at its client configuration endpoint (RFC 7592) using the registration access token.

## oidc logout

Run RP-Initiated Logout: build the end_session request, send the browser there and wait on a loopback post-logout redirect to confirm the provider returns with the same state. With url_only it just builds the URL.

MCP tool: `oidc_logout`. Opens a browser and waits for a person.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer URL; endpoints and keys are discovered from its metadata. |
| `--client-id` | string | OAuth client identifier. |
| `--end-session-endpoint` | string | End session endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--id-token-hint` | string | ID token previously issued to this client (recommended). CLI: `@path` reads a file, `-` reads stdin. |
| `--logout-hint` | string | Hint about the user who is logging out. |
| `--post-logout-redirect-uri` | string | Where the provider should send the browser afterwards; must be registered and, to be captured, point at this machine. Default `http://localhost:8765/logged-out`. |
| `--url-only` | bool | Only build and return the logout URL. |
| `--open-browser` | bool | Open the system browser automatically. Default `true`. |
| `--wait` | int | Seconds to wait for the person to finish in the browser. Default `180`. |

Plus the parameters [every oidc operation](#every-oidc-operation) takes and the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).

## oidc bcp_probe

Probe what an authorization server enforces of the OAuth 2.0 Security BCP (RFC 9700) by sending requests it must refuse: redirect URIs that differ from the registered one, the implicit grant, a framed sign-in page, wrong and downgraded PKCE, a replayed authorization code and a replayed refresh token. Uses the same client and loopback redirect URI as oidc login. The PKCE and replay probes need a sign-in each; after the first, the provider's session usually completes them without asking.

MCP tool: `oidc_bcp_probe`. **Changes data at the remote system.** Opens a browser and waits for a person.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--issuer` | string | Issuer URL; endpoints and keys are discovered from its metadata. |
| `--client-id` | string | OAuth client identifier. |
| `--client-secret` | string | Client secret (prefer env IDPDBG_CLIENT_SECRET or a profile). Secret: falls back to `IDPDBG_CLIENT_SECRET`, redacted in traces. |
| `--client-auth` | string | Client authentication method; default basic when a secret is set, otherwise none. One of `basic`, `post`, `none`, `private_key_jwt`, `client_secret_jwt`, `tls_client_auth`, `self_signed_tls_client_auth`. |
| `--token-endpoint` | string | Token endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--client-key` | string | Client private key (PEM inline or a path) for private_key_jwt and signed request objects. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--client-key-id` | string | kid to put in the header of JWTs signed with client_key. |
| `--signing-alg` | string | JWS algorithm for client_key; default follows the key type (RS256, ES256, EdDSA); use PS256 for RSA-PSS. |
| `--client-assertion-aud` | string | aud of the client assertion; default is the issuer, else the endpoint being called. |
| `--mtls-cert` | string | Client certificate (PEM inline or a path) for mutual TLS. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--mtls-key` | string | Private key for mtls_cert (PEM inline or a path). May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--dpop` | bool | Send DPoP proofs (RFC 9449) so issued tokens are bound to a key. |
| `--dpop-key` | string | DPoP private key (PEM inline or a path); default is a fresh P-256 key that lasts for this run only. May be a file path (CLI or profile only). |
| `--authorization-endpoint` | string | Authorization endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--scope` | string | Space-separated scopes. Default `openid profile email`. |
| `--response-type` | string | code (default), or an implicit/hybrid type such as 'code id_token'. Default `code`. |
| `--response-mode` | string | query, fragment or form_post. |
| `--pkce` | bool | Send an S256 PKCE challenge. Default `true`. |
| `--prompt` | string | none, login, consent or select_account. |
| `--login-hint` | string | Login hint passed to the provider. |
| `--acr-values` | string | Requested authentication context class references. |
| `--max-age` | int | Maximum authentication age in seconds. |
| `--audience` | string | audience parameter (Auth0-style APIs). |
| `--resource` | string | RFC 8707 resource indicator. |
| `--extra` | json | Extra authorization parameters as a JSON object, e.g. {"claims":"..."}. |
| `--par` | bool | Push the authorization request to the PAR endpoint first (RFC 9126) and send only its request_uri through the browser. |
| `--jar` | bool | Send the authorization parameters as a request object signed with client_key (RFC 9101). |
| `--pushed-authorization-request-endpoint` | string | PAR endpoint, overriding discovery. |
| `--redirect-host` | string | Host used in the redirect URI (localhost or 127.0.0.1). Default `localhost`. |
| `--redirect-port` | int | Loopback port to listen on. Default `8765`. |
| `--redirect-path` | string | Path of the redirect URI. Default `/callback`. |
| `--redirect-uri` | string | Full redirect URI, overriding host/port/path; must point at this machine. |
| `--open-browser` | bool | Open the system browser automatically. Default `true`. |
| `--wait` | int | Seconds to wait for the person to finish in the browser. Default `180`. |
| `--probes` | list | Probes to run: redirect_uri (exact matching of the redirect URI), implicit (response_type=token refused), clickjacking (the sign-in page cannot be framed), pkce (a wrong code_verifier is refused), pkce_downgrade (a code_verifier is refused for a code requested without code_challenge), code_replay (a code works only once), refresh_replay (a rotated refresh token stops working). The first three need no sign-in. With fapi, also par_required (a request without PAR is refused), par_client_auth (PAR without client authentication is refused), par_redirect_uri (PAR without redirect_uri is refused), dpop_code_binding (a code bound to one DPoP key is refused with another) and code_lifetime (a code is refused after 61 seconds). Default `redirect_uri,implicit,clickjacking,pkce,pkce_downgrade,code_replay,refresh_replay`. |

Plus the parameters [every oidc operation](#every-oidc-operation) takes and the [common parameters](README.md#common-parameters).
